title: Famil Door and Roads
statementMd:
Famil Door’s City map looks like a tree (undirected connected acyclic graph) so other people call it Treeland. There are $*n*$ intersections in the city connected by $*n* - 1$ bidirectional roads.

There are $*m*$ friends of Famil Door living in the city. The $*i*$-th friend lives at the intersection $*u*_{*i*}$ and works at the intersection $*v*_{*i*}$. Everyone in the city is unhappy because there is exactly one simple path between their home and work.

Famil Door plans to construct exactly one new road and he will randomly choose one among $*n*·(*n* - 1) / 2$ possibilities. Note, that he may even build a new road between two cities that are already connected by one.

He knows, that each of his friends will become happy, if after Famil Door constructs a new road there is a path from this friend home to work and back that doesn't visit the same road twice. Formally, there is a simple cycle containing both $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$.

Moreover, if the friend becomes happy, his pleasure is equal to the length of such path (it's easy to see that it's unique). For each of his friends Famil Door wants to know his expected pleasure, that is the expected length of the cycle containing both $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ if we consider only cases when such a cycle exists.

## Input

The first line of the input contains integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($2 ≤ *n*,  *m* ≤ 100 000$) — the number of the intersections in the Treeland and the number of Famil Door's friends.

Then follow $*n* - 1$ lines describing bidirectional roads. Each of them contains two integers $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*)$ — the indices of intersections connected by the $*i*$-th road.

Last $*m*$ lines of the input describe Famil Door's friends. The $*i*$-th of these lines contain two integers $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*, *u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$) — indices of intersections where the $*i*$-th friend lives and works.

## Output

For each friend you should print the expected value of pleasure if he will be happy. Your answer will be considered correct if its absolute or relative error does not exceed $10^{ - 6}$.

Namely: let's assume that your answer is $*a*$, and the answer of the jury is $*b*$. The checker program will consider your answer correct, if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c1b52f0e83e1008ebbb127cf309e0d965533b043.png).

## Note

Consider the second sample.

1. Both roads $(1, 2)$ and $(2, 3)$ work, so the expected length if ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ec563337e40cadafa8449c9571eb5b8c7199e10c.png)
2. Roads $(1, 3)$ and $(2, 3)$ make the second friend happy. Same as for friend $1$ the answer is $2.5$
3. The only way to make the third friend happy is to add road $(2, 3)$, so the answer is $3$
statementZhMd:
Famil Door 的城市地图看起来像一棵树（无向连通无环图），因此其他人称其为 Treeland。城市中有 $*n*$ 个路口，由 $*n* - 1$ 条双向道路连接。

Famil Door 有 $*m*$ 位朋友住在这座城市中。第 $*i*$ 位朋友住在路口 $*u*_{*i*}$，并在路口 $*v*_{*i*}$ 工作。城市中的每个人都对此感到不满，因为他们的家和工作地点之间恰好只有一条简单路径。

Famil Door 计划恰好修建一条新道路，并从 $*n*·(*n* - 1) / 2$ 种可能性中随机选择一种。注意，他甚至可以在已经有道路直接连接的两个路口之间修建新道路。

他知道，如果 Famil Door 修建新道路后，某位朋友的家和工作地点之间存在一条往返路径，且这条路径不会重复经过同一条道路，那么这位朋友就会感到开心。形式化地说，就是存在一个同时包含 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$ 的简单环。

此外，如果这位朋友感到开心，他的快乐值等于这样一条路径的长度（不难看出，这样的路径是唯一的）。对于每位朋友，Famil Door 想知道他的期望快乐值，也就是只考虑存在这样的环的情况时，同时包含 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$ 的环的长度的期望值。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$2 ≤ *n*,  *m* ≤ 100 000$）——Treeland 中路口的数量以及 Famil Door 的朋友数量。

接下来 $*n* - 1$ 行描述双向道路。每行包含两个整数 $*a*_{*i*}$ 和 $*b*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$）——第 $*i*$ 条道路所连接的路口编号。

最后 $*m*$ 行描述 Famil Door 的朋友。第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$，$*u*_{*i*} ≠ *v*_{*i*}$）——第 $*i*$ 位朋友居住和工作的路口编号。

## 输出格式

对于每位朋友，如果他会感到开心，请输出其快乐值的期望值。如果你的答案的绝对误差或相对误差不超过 $10^{ - 6}$，则会被判定为正确。

具体来说，假设你的答案为 $*a*$，标准答案为 $*b*$。若满足 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/c1b52f0e83e1008ebbb127cf309e0d965533b043.png)，评测程序将认为你的答案正确。

## 说明

考虑第二个样例。

1. 道路 $(1, 2)$ 和 $(2, 3)$ 都可行，因此期望长度为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ec563337e40cadafa8449c9571eb5b8c7199e10c.png)
2. 道路 $(1, 3)$ 和 $(2, 3)$ 会使第二位朋友感到开心。与第 $1$ 位朋友相同，答案为 $2.5$。
3. 使第三位朋友感到开心的唯一方法是添加道路 $(2, 3)$，因此答案为 $3$。
